note: Upper-floor panoramic lounge of the Rotunda on Chopok as in the 2016 photo: camera ~1.6 m high on the lounge floor, looking at the gently curved window wall (left two thirds) and the natural-stone core wall (right third); horizon y ~470; the dark blue window sofas, the exhibition furniture and the stone wall stand on y ~700-728 (~126 px per metre there). Perspective s(y) = (y - 470) / 545. The windows show the real north view (the Funitel line with its pylons going down, guideposts, the Liptov basin, the High Tatras on the horizon) with June snow patches near the summit. The Atlas exhibition 2035: the normalisation panel on its stand, the bell showcase, the empty frame on the stone wall, the door to the stairs down to the plateau (Atlas pavilion); the lounge continues out of the left edge to the Funitel station. The third-party lift-parts sculpture of the photo is left out. The walk polygon leaves out the two table groups with their tub chairs (feet y ~777) and the panel stand (feet y ~750). Base painting v3 (v1 plus a closed album on a stand in the showcase, for the Q3D causal effect).
